inventory.story: Hartwig, German. I only used it to hang the shelves.
My cousin brought it from Moscow. Still had the film on the screen.
Grandad’s. It still drills, no batteries needed.
It's old but it works. The battery lasts till lunch.
Mum’s old phone. She got a new one and I got custody of this one.
His grandfather’s army watch. Pawned until the foreman pays.
My mother’s bracelet. Don’t look at me like that, I always come back.
Grandfather’s. He never spoke about it. I wrote a poem about him never speaking about it. It’s quite long.
I need the bus fare home. Truly.
They’re very old. Older than the dinosaurs, the beads, I mean.
I wore it to my exams for luck. I passed them all.
Dima’s present when Mishutka was born. He’ll be back in two weeks. Not the earrings. Dima. Well, both.

item.story: My confirmation cross. I believed until Vova. Now I believe in the post office, which at least arrives.
The ring again. It knows the way here better than I do.
Issued to my father in the army. Officers only, those dials.
I won it in a raffle at work. I already have a phone.
Bought it last September, before term. It's barely a year old.
It brings good health. Not to me, apparently.
For the Victory Day parade my son wants a new phone. So.
I need it gone by Friday. Rent.
Proof condition. It says so on the plastic. Well, the plastic broke.
Dagestani gold. My grandmother’s. Heavier than it looks, like all of us. For the wedding hall deposit.
A wedding present. The marriage did not last, the coin did.
My mother’s earrings. I never wear them now. My ears have given up.
My telephone. It only calls. My mother only answers, so it is enough. But the foreman has not paid, so.
Issued to my father in the army. Officers only, those dials.

news.headline: Hydrological bureau publishes its spring water chart
news.body: The bureau’s chart of the river’s spring levels is pinned up at every tram stop. Nobody can read it. Pensioners hold it up to the light anyway and say, darkly, that they remember worse.

item.story: Kladez Hunter, the good one. You can find coins from Catherine’s time with it.
Better than a bank. Banks go bust. Gold does not.
The bear mascot cried at the closing ceremony. I cried too. Anyway, the coin.

queue.line: Please, just a loan. I’ll be back for it, I swear, I just need to get through this month.
My brother writes poems. Did you know? A little book, printed at his own cost, sixty copies. He sold one to a library and gave the rest away and one of them ended up on my bench, left by a tourist.

item.story: My mother kept it in a biscuit tin. She died in the winter.
My watch. They gave it back to me at the gate with my belt and my laces. It stopped the day I went in and started again the day I came out. I wound it, but still.

queue.line: Afternoon. Tuesday meeting tonight. We sit in a circle and drink tea and don’t do things. It’s harder than it sounds. My watch. They gave it back to me at the gate with my belt and my laces. It stopped the day I went in and started again the day I came out. I wound it, but still.

lines: Good day. I came to say goodbye, for the summer. I am going home to Urgut. My mother has found me a wife. I have seen her photograph; she has seen mine. We were both disappointed and both said yes.
In the autumn I come back. Bakhtiyor says the next building is twelve floors. I will carry every brick and think of my wife and this city, and which is colder.
